Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the AetherCloud Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in listen-only mode. After the presentation, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star then one on your telephone keypad. If using a speakerphone, please pick up the handset before pressing the keys. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us. Today, we will be discussing AetherCloud's results for the Q2 2024. With me on the call are Johnathan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Technology Officer; and Michael Tran, Chief Product Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call contains forward-looking statements. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. AetherCloud had an exceptional Q2, exceeding expectations across all key metrics. This success is a testament to our innovative technology, dedicated team, and strong customer relationships.

During the quarter, we focused on five key areas:
1. Expanding our market share in key verticals.
2. Investing in cutting-edge research and development.
3. Enhancing our cloud security posture.
4. Driving operational efficiencies.
5. Strengthening our ecosystem partnerships.

Let me highlight our standout accomplishments from Q2 FY2024 and lay out the strategic priorities that will propel us forward. In a fiercely competitive cloud computing arena, where hyperscalers such as AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud are advancing AI infrastructure, and enterprises demand hybrid multi-cloud setups despite economic pressures, we've not only held our ground but gained momentum with impressive growth and share expansion.

On the financial front, Q2 revenue hit $8.7 billion, reflecting 29% year-over-year growth and 8% sequential increase, surpassing the midpoint of our guidance. This momentum came from a 35% YoY rise in Annual Recurring Revenue to $32.1 billion, with Remaining Performance Obligations reaching a record $112 billion, up 42% YoY—our best RPO performance in three years. Non-GAAP operating margins improved to 32.4%, gaining 210 basis points, thanks to leverage from scaling data centers and cutting per-unit compute costs by 15% via custom silicon optimizations similar to AWS Graviton or Google TPUs.

Customer wins highlighted our enterprise traction: we onboarded 1,450 new customers sequentially, including 78 Fortune 500 names, like a top U.S. bank shifting core banking to our Sovereign Cloud and a prominent European automaker using Aether AI Foundry for GenAI training. ARR from large customers over $1 million annually jumped 52% YoY to $18.5 billion, comprising 58% of total ARR. Net Revenue Retention stayed solid at 118%, showing robust expansion in base accounts with sticky data lakes and real-time analytics.

From a product standpoint, IaaS revenue climbed 31% YoY, boosted by 25% higher GPU utilization via NVIDIA H100 integrations and our upcoming Aether TensorCore accelerators. PaaS surged 40%, with Aether Kubernetes Service managing over 2.5 million clusters worldwide, surpassing Azure Kubernetes in managed containers according to recent Gartner reports. SaaS via Aether DataMesh grew 55% YoY, taking share from Snowflake and Databricks with zero-ETL and multi-cloud federated querying.

Geographically, North America, at 52% of revenue, grew 32% YoY, driven by AI demand from Big Tech LLM builds. APAC hit $2.1 billion, up 38%, with rapid 95% utilization in new Mumbai and Tokyo-2 regions meeting data sovereignty under India's DPDP Act. EMEA advanced 22%, offset by GDPR costs but bolstered by UK public sector deals via IL5 certification equivalent to FedRAMP High. LATAM added $450 million, up 50%, supporting fintech growth in São Paulo.

We also advanced sustainability, dropping portfolio carbon intensity 28% YoY with 65% renewable energy and liquid cooling in 45 data centers, exceeding AWS benchmarks and aligning with EU CSRD.

Moving to priorities, we're honing in on three pillars: AI ubiquity, global edge expansion, and sustainable hyperscale. For AI, $5 billion FY2024 capex—75% AI-focused—brings Aether GenAI Studio to GA in Q3, a managed platform like Vertex AI or Bedrock with RAG and fine-tuning on 1.2 exaFLOP clusters. We've locked 500 MW NVIDIA GB200 through 2026, aiming for 40% compute from inference by FY2025 in the $200 billion GenAI market per McKinsey.

Edge expansion adds 150 zones by year-end for 5G/6G with Verizon and Vodafone, hitting 75ms latencies for AR/VR and AV data per IDC's 60% edge shift. Sustainable hyperscale commissions 12 new regions FY2025 in ASEAN and Middle East, with NuScale SMRs for carbon-neutral power, targeting 100% renewable match by 2027 and PUE to 1.08.

These efforts position us for 150 bps IaaS share gain this year, guiding FY2024 revenue to $35.2-$35.8 billion in a 22% CAGR market through 2028 per Synergy Research.

Now I'll turn the call over to Sarah Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan. As Johnathan mentioned, we had a stellar financial performance in the Q2. Revenue grew by 29% year-over-year to $8.7 billion, significantly outpacing industry averages. Our gross margin was 68.4%, reflecting our pricing power and efficient cost management. Our operating margin was 32.4%.

Good afternoon, everyone. Let me break down our top-line performance, which highlights the robustness of our cloud platform against rising AI workloads and multi-cloud strategies.

For Q2 ended June 30, 2024, total revenue came in at $8.7 billion, a strong 29% increase from $6.7 billion in Q2 FY2023. This beat the high end of our $8.4 to $8.6 billion guidance by about 1.2%, or $100 million. FX-neutral growth was 30%, showing recurring stream strength despite high interest rates and cautious enterprise budgets.

Year-to-date revenue is $17.2 billion, on track for the upper half of full-year outlook. This is our 15th consecutive quarter of double-digit growth, beating IDC's 17% IaaS/PaaS global rate. Share gains versus AWS and Azure stem from competitive NVIDIA H100 pricing and QuantumForge AI early access with 500+ enterprise sign-ups.

By segment:
Infrastructure Services (IaaS)—compute, storage, networking—reached $4.6 billion, up 27% YoY, driven by 25% HPC utilization for GenAI training. AetherEdge nodes in 15 metro centers added $140 million, as a major U.S. automaker moved inference to our low-latency setup.

Platform and Developer Services (PaaS) hit $2.5 billion, up 32% YoY, with 30% growth in AetherKube container workloads for Fortune 500 DevOps. A multi-year European telco deal layered PaaS on bare-metal for 5G core.

Data, AI, and Analytics exploded to $1.4 billion, 38% YoY and 16% of revenue (up from 13%), powered by AetherML with TPUs and Hugging Face ties, adding $360 million net new ARR. Aether-Llama-70B usage quadrupled QoQ, like Google Vertex AI trends.

Other Services, including cybersecurity SaaS, contributed $120 million, up 18% YoY from managed bundles.

Regionally:
Americas (72%): $6.3 billion, +31% YoY, led by U.S. hyperscalers and Big Tech like Meta-scale clusters; AI was 40% of bookings.
EMEA (18%): $1.6 billion, +26% YoY, with Frankfurt-3/Paris-2 sovereign regions winning DAX 40 banks despite data rules.
APAC (10%): $870 million, +24% YoY FX-neutral, Japan/India led, Mumbai-2 grabbing $60 million gov migrations.

This backs our $12 billion FY2024 capex for 20 AI zones and 500 MW liquid-cooled GPUs. RPO up 24% YoY to $145 billion, 85% multi-year. Q3 bookings up 8%, guiding $9.0-$9.3 billion revenue, 28-30% YoY.

Risks include GPU shortages from Blackwell, Azure OpenAI pricing, longer non-AI cycles. Free cash flow margin at 28% supports buybacks, M&A like serverless observability.

Q2 cements our multi-trillion cloud leadership—AI demand is structural.

Now, I'll hand it over to Dr. Elena Vasquez for a technical update.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah. From a technology perspective, we made significant strides in several key areas this quarter. We are proud to announce the general availability of our new AetherForge platform, which offers unparalleled performance and scalability.

I'll now discuss our customer churn rate and retention trends, which highlight the stickiness of the AetherCloud platform in a crowded field with hyperscalers like AWS, Azure, Google Cloud in infra, and Snowflake, Databricks in data/AI. Retention is our moat, measured by Net Revenue Retention—or NRR—covering expansions despite contractions.

For Q2 FY2024, dollar-based NRR was 119%, up 200 bps QoQ and 400 bps YoY—11th quarter over 115%, beating public cloud peers' 110% per Bessemer benchmarks. This spans our $8.2 billion trailing ARR, with expansions at 28% of revenue from AI/ML upsells.

Gross dollar retention was 96%, retaining 96 cents per prior ARR dollar sans expansions, via 68% 3+ year deals (up from 52% two years ago). Logo churn annualized at 3.2%, down from 4.1% YoY, below 5-7% SaaS median per KeyBanc.

By segment, enterprise (> $1M ARR, 72% ARR) hit 128% NRR from Kubernetes containers and AetherAI inference. Contractions under 2% via "Cloud Health Score" predicting risks 45 days early. Mid-market/SMB (>$100K) at 112% NRR, stabilized by FinOps tiered pricing amid macro pressures.

Regionally: North America (58% ARR) 2.8% churn, 122% NRR, strong in finance/healthcare with FedRAMP High/HITRAMP; NeoBank Financial tripled banking on confidential enclaves, 40% TCO savings vs. AWS Nitro.

EMEA (22% ARR) 4.1% churn, 116% NRR despite GDPR/energy costs; Frankfurt/Paris sovereign clouds and Palo Alto ZTNA lifted retention 15%.

APAC (15%) 3.5% churn, 125% NRR up YoY; Singapore/Tokyo edges for 5G/AI, AsiaWave Telecom moved 5PB IoT from Alibaba; China via Marketplace with 450+ ISVs.

Latin America (5%) 5.2% churn, 108% NRR; spot pricing reversed 60% contractions.

Drivers: Tech like Q1 AetherForge serverless on eBPF cut egress churn 22%; 42% customers used AetherML Llama 3, $180M new ARR; Nitro-like root-of-trust stopped 95% ransomware per SOC 2.

Customer success: "Retention Engine" on 15M daily signals, 3x ROI; 2022 cohorts now 94% retained.

Tailwinds: Multi-cloud fatigue (Gartner 62% want "cloud-smart"); OpenTelemetry won 120 Datadog migrants, +18% retention; AI scaling avoids bill shock.

Ahead: Q3 NRR 118-120%, churn to 3% FYE with $500M RPO. 99.999% SLA, concierge mitigate price wars/OpenStack.

Our metrics confirm AetherCloud's enterprise essentiality—we're expanding steadily.

I'll now pass it to Michael Tran for a product roadmap update.

Michael Tran:
Thank you, Elena. This quarter, we launched Aether GenAI Studio, a game-changing solution for enterprise AI/ML workloads. Early customer feedback has been overwhelmingly positive. We are seeing strong demand and a rapid increase in adoption.

Today, let me unpack our overall gross margin trends and the drivers fueling them, as they demonstrate our platform's scalability where COGS ties to data center depreciation, power, bandwidth, and CDN.

In Q2, GAAP gross margin rose 320 bps YoY to 68.4%, sixth straight sequential gain. Non-GAAP at 69.2%, up 280 bps YoY, 90 bps QoQ—outpacing AWS's 66%, Azure's 68%. Revenue $8.7 billion yielded record $5.9 billion gross profit.

Over eight quarters, margins climbed from 62.1% in Q4 FY22 amid supply issues/crypto unwind.

Four drivers: product mix, infra optimization, capacity, regions.

Product mix (200 bps): AI/ML via Vortex AI at 82% margins now 32% revenue (from 18%); NexPod containers 72%, Quantum Lambda serverless 78%, cyber SaaS 85% up 45%. Mix added 450 bps over two years, offset by IaaS promos.

Infra efficiencies (150 bps): Graviton4 ARM in 65% new capacity, 35% better perf/$ vs x86, 28% ECU savings; Trainium2 cuts AI COGS 40% vs A100s. PUE 1.12 via liquid cooling in 40% of 150+ DCs, 92% renewables hedging Europe 15% power spike; CDN/peering cut bandwidth 22%; rack depreciation down 18% on $12B CapEx.

Capacity utilization 87% from 76%, AI demand; ML forecasting cuts idle; supply lead times 9 months, 1.2 GW FY24.

Regions: NA (55%) 71.5% on Mag7/finance z/VM; EMEA (25%) 68% despite Data Act, H100 Frankfurt/Paris; APAC (15%) 63% on expansions but Japan +50% util via SoftBank to 68% YE; LatAm/MEA 60%.

"Margin 70" targets $2B efficiencies FY25: edge micros 75%+, sovereign India/Brazil. Pricing: AI credits 200 bps invest, enclaves +20%.

Headwinds modest: Oracle Gen2 pricing, $28B CapEx (125% rev) dilutes till 90% util. RPO +35% de-risks.

Guide Q3 68.8-69.4% non-GAAP, FY24 68.7% (+450 bps); path to 72%+ as AI 45%, PUE <1.10 in $800B 22% CAGR TAM per Gartner.

Now, back to Johnathan Hale.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you, Michael. We are incredibly excited about the future. We believe our investments in innovation, our commitment to customer success, and our talented team will continue to drive strong growth and value creation.

As we peer into FY25 and beyond, macroeconomic influences shape our guidance. While Q2 showed resilience with 29% revenue growth to $8.7 billion and 35% cloud ARR to $32.1 billion, we're tackling high rates, inflation, geopolitics.

Tailwinds: GenAI boom—StratoAI with H100s grew AI compute 45% QoQ to 18% revenue, to 25% FY25 end via StratoForge edge cutting latency 60% for AV/IoT. Digital transformation solid, RPO +35% to $42 billion from F500 finance/healthcare at 40% TCO savings.

Headwinds: 5.25-5.50% U.S. rates elongate cycles 5-7% in < $10M non-AI; energy inflation 12% YoY, PUE 1.15 hedged 65% renewables on 25 GW.

Regions: NA (62%) 30% FY25 growth on Mag7/SMB FlexScale +22%, fed caps -2-3% public. EMEA (18%) 18-22%, ECB 4.5%/energy; sovereign wins €1.2B DAX but French tax +1-2%. APAC (15%) 25-28% India/5G, Singapore/Tokyo +40%, USD JPY145 shaves 3%. LatAm/ROW (5%) 20% nearshoring.

Geopol: Chip controls delay QuantumCore 3-6 months, 5% AI hit; 70% supply diversified.

Mitigations: OptiCloud Advisor saves 25-35% hybrid, 80% pilots to 118% NRR like Siemens/JPM. Capex $12-14B (15% rev), AI focus, EBITDA 38-40%. $500M green DCs to 80% renewable 2026, +15% EU RFPs.

EdgeNova acquisition adds $800M ARR 5G. $15B cash, no maturities, $0.50/share dividend growth. Macro tempers to 20-25% low end FY25, but AI/execution beats peers.

With that, let's open the call for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, if you would like to ask a question, please press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from Ben Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Ben Thompson:
Thanks for taking my question. Johnathan, your NRR looks impressive at 119%. Can you elaborate on what specific technical innovations are driving that expansion, particularly in enterprise, and how sustainable is it with macro pressures?

Johnathan Hale:
Thanks, Ben. Great question. As Elena detailed, our 119% NRR, especially 128% in enterprise, stems from integrations like Kubernetes containers and AetherAI inference, plus tools like Cloud Health Score for early risk detection. AetherForge serverless has slashed egress churn by 22%, and GenAI activations added $180 million ARR. With multi-year deals at 68% and proactive success programs, it's sustainable—Q3 guide 118-120%, enterprise offsetting SMB softness. Macro hasn't dented our top-decile SLA or concierge support.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Hi, team. Sarah, congrats on the margin expansion. What gives you confidence in hitting 68.8-69.4% next quarter, especially with CapEx intensity?

Sarah Chen:
Thanks, Lisa. Confidence comes from mix shift to 82% margin AI now 32% revenue, Graviton4 efficiencies cutting costs 28%, and utilization to 87%. PUE 1.12 and renewables hedge energy. CapEx $28 billion FY24 dilutes short-term but ramps with RPO backlog. "Margin 70" efficiencies and pricing discipline on premiums like enclaves support the guide, positioning for 72%+ medium-term.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Raj Patel with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Raj Patel:
Thanks. Elena, on the macro side, how are you thinking about GPU supply and its impact on AI growth?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Raj, thanks. We've secured ample H100/GB200 capacity, but Blackwell ramps could constrain—mitigated by Trainium2 alternatives cutting COGS 40%. Supply diversification to Samsung/TSMC limits delays to 5% AI revenue. Our elastic scaling and open models keep us ahead in inference demand.

Johnathan Hale:
Thank you for your insightful questions and your continued interest in AetherCloud. We remain focused on executing our strategy and delivering long-term value for our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the call.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
